fields.direction: conservative
fields.proposed_fix: FIX-A
fields.note: The card's member force N = pRs/2 is the two-way arch resultant, but the frame it counts has M = 3V-6 members of length s. Statics fix their mean compression at 4*pi*R^3*p/(M*s) = pRs/(2*sqrt3) exactly (virial identity). The card's own Et=(2/sqrt3)EA/s with nu=1/3 gives the same strain. Geodesic trusses of 162 and 362 nodes solved by statics (rank complete, residual 6e-15) give mean C/(pRl/(2*sqrt3)) = 1.017 and 1.007, with a maximum of 600 kN at mean l 2.0 m. Each member carries 0.289*s^2 of film, not s^2/2. The force is inherited from MAINLINE-002's P3 rule (COMMON.md). Yield, Euler, local and Perry are sqrt3-conservative at a given tube. Re-optimised, SiC on the equilateral grid at k 0.2 is 1.408 and 6061 is 0.339. The member-end load at s 2.04 m is 562 kN, not 974 kN (022, 023).
fields.fix: FIX-A: score the P3 members with N = pRs/(2*sqrt3) on the equilateral frame, or count a true two-way frame (M = 2V, V = 4*pi*R^2/s^2), then re-optimise.

fields.direction: optimistic
fields.proposed_fix: FIX-B
fields.note: Local buckling keeps gamma = 1 at r/t 140.5. NASA SP-8007, the source 011 cites for the 0.6, gives gamma = 1-0.901*(1-exp(-sqrt(r/t)/16)) = 0.529. Local at the card's SiC point is then 0.648. Re-optimised with gamma, SiC on the equilateral grid at k 0.2 is 1.075 (r/t 94), two-way is 0.967, and with FIX-A as well 1.205 and 1.083. At 100 kg systems and a 5% margin these are 1.130 and 1.015.
fields.fix: FIX-B: apply SP-8007's gamma to the local mode and re-optimise.

fields.direction: optimistic (condition)
fields.note: The smeared D (Buchert's t_B) presumes members continuous in bending through the nodes, which means moment-rigid joints. With pinned or soft nodes the bending stiffness and the global mode fall, so 023's joints must carry member-end moments as well as axial force. Member torsion is omitted; with torsion-rigid joints it would raise the global SF by 13.7% for SiC (nu 0.14) and 11.8% for 6061 (lattice sum D1111 1.454 or 1.407 against 1.125).

fields.direction: informational (022)
fields.note: At the SiC point the L/1000 imperfection adds +/-58.8 MPa (eta 0.0332, amplifier 1.240) to 1.428 GPa of compression. The fibres are at -1.487 and -1.370 GPa, so there is no tension, and with FIX-A they are -0.855 and -0.794 GPa. The 380 MPa flexural scan (0.262) is therefore not the arcs' allowable. The open number is the compressive design allowable of a 0.88 mm brittle wall at about 1.4 GPa of service stress (022's Weibull item).

fields.direction: possibly optimistic at k 0.4
fields.note: Wright's 'modified k of 0.4' may be the coefficient in p = k*E*(t/R)^2, where classical is 2/sqrt(3(1-nu^2)) = 1.2247 at nu 1/3. That would be about 0.327 of classical, not 0.4, and the k 0.4 global pressures would fall by about 18%. The citation is confirmed in Buchert 1965's bibliography. The Table 2 expression is needed.

fields.direction: documentation

fields.direction: ranking depends on the rule
fields.note: The CR-1457 step rule gives aramid (Vc 3.1-3.5) the optimistic gamma 1 and aluminium (Vc 0.5-0.6) the conservative 0.2. Applied to both families, 018's optimistic curve (PROJECTION) gives aluminium 0.847 against aramid 0.609 on the optimistic line, 0.924 against 0.650 at 5% and 0.988 against 0.685 at 0%, where aluminium is capped by Be face compression. 018's conservative curve gives 0.557 against 0.253, 0.617 against 0.270 and 0.669 against 0.284. 'Aramid leads' on every margin line rests on the mixed pairing. The budgets were not re-solved under the curves.

fields.direction: documentation

fields.factor: zero margin raises the structural budget by (lift-100)/(0.95*lift-100), about 5 percent, which does not close a wrinkling gap of several times

fields.direction: MAINLINE-012's equal-margin geometry, when that card is the newer input.

fields.gap: Joint and seam mass at the 009 SiC point: 89.2 to 3004.3 kg across panel sizes 4 m to 0.25 m, against the 216.427 kg five percent allowance. Only 4 m panels, which do not exist in SiC today (PROJECTION), fit; today's 0.5 m Hexoloy plate size is 330 to 694 percent of the allowance; conservative 0.25 m tiling leaves the hull 966 to 2543 kg heavy.
fields.direction: Pin the real maximum Hexoloy SA plate size from the manufacturer, and produce a seam parts list (doubler, adhesive, core splice) for a named panel size; or re-run the point on a face family whose sheet widths are 2 to 4 m today (aluminium, CFRP layup).
fields.effect: Decides alone whether the 009 point floats; up to 1388 percent of the joint allowance.

fields.gap: Lift at the site: dL/L = dp/p - dT/T. A QUESTIONABLE hot summer afternoon at +25.1 K takes the margin to -186.3 kg; 0.1 mm of retained water is 125.6 kg, 51 percent of the margin; 1 mm is 1257 kg. No site is named anywhere in the mainline, so the 5 percent margin has no climate envelope.
fields.direction: Name the operating site and season windows; size a ballast or trim system for the hot-day deficit; require a hydrophobic coating and a shedding check before flight; weigh the hull after rain.
fields.effect: Margin negative at the hot extreme without these; climbing does not recover it (lift falls about 9.4 percent per km).

fields.gap: CTE mismatch SiC 4.5e-6 vs PVC 60e-6 per K drives sandwich shear-lag at 283 kPa per 30 K face-core difference (567 kPa at 60 K), against a QUESTIONABLE H35 shear strength of 0.40 to 0.55 MPa: one-off SF 1.41 to 1.94 at 30 K, 0.71 to 0.97 at 60 K, cycled daily. Not one of the five scored modes; no fatigue law.
fields.direction: Bond-line and core shear coupon under thermal cycling over the full daily band; pin DIAB H35 shear strength and modulus; add the mismatch mode to the scored set.
fields.effect: A new structural failure mode at the 009 point, unquantified for the life of the hull.

fields.gap: Holding p_int at a 1000 Pa ceiling takes 46.3 L/s there, 527 to 844 W real, and a QUESTIONABLE 150 to 400 kg pump set: 61 to 164 percent of the whole 244.472 kg float margin. The ceiling itself is an owner assumption; commissioning pump-down is 506 kWh.
fields.direction: Shop a real Roots or screw pump specification at this duty (mass, power, intake pressure curve); set the operational p_int ceiling from the leak budget; consider distributed smaller pumps or a ground-only pump.
fields.effect: Trades directly against the margin; can exceed it entirely at the conservative end.

fields.gap: Resident moisture 0.5 to 3 percent of the 2208.2 kg PVC core is 11.0 to 66.2 kg of water, worth 347 to 2079 Pa inside if released, against the 954.6 Pa one-percent-per-day ceiling. Steady outgassing itself is only 0.00 to 0.03 percent of the leak budget.
fields.direction: Measure water content of the core lot; specify a bake-out and vent procedure at commissioning with a dry-gas backfill during assembly.
fields.effect: Without bake-out the moisture alone can exceed the one-percent ceiling after release.

fields.gap: The 1 percent-per-day budget equals a 2.48 mm2 choked hole or 4.25 mm2 molecular aperture: vacuum integrity at this budget is a discrete-defect and detection problem, not a material one. No leak specification, no detection threshold, no in-service pressure telemetry is defined.
fields.direction: Set an operational leak spec well inside 46.28 Pa m3/s with margin; specify seam leak testing per panel at assembly and a pressure sensor resolution able to see a fraction of the budget.
fields.effect: Detection latency decides whether the trim pump is a convenience or a life-limit.

fields.gap: Mooring design load 48.3 kN at 20 m/s with a 1.4 gust factor; a bare 0.0707 m2 hardpoint patch sees 683 kPa against a 500.0 kPa QUESTIONABLE core allowable, SF 0.73. Added air mass 2445 kg equals hull mass, so snatch loads need a dynamic mooring analysis.
fields.direction: Design spreaders of at least 0.145 m2 per hardpoint for core SF 1.5; run the mooring dynamics with the added mass; qualify six hardpoints, about 48 kg.
fields.effect: Local design plus about 20 percent of the margin in fittings; not a hull-mode problem.

fields.gap: Ground handling of a 4645 kg, 20 m vacuum sphere has no concept, cradle, or transport plan; core-safe pad pressure target is 250 kPa or less, and any handling dent is an imperfection feeding the already-severe 0.20 knockdown.
fields.direction: Specify cradle geometry and pad pressure; define a dimensional inspection and imperfection survey after every move, tied to the knockdown basis.
fields.effect: A dent below the survey threshold enters the buckling knockdown unmeasured.

fields.gap: The thermal balance averages sky (260 to 275 K) and ground radiation and gives a no-convection bound of 313.5 K, under the QUESTIONABLE H35 service limit 343 to 353 K; but a hot apron, heat island, or hangar radiates from the ground side and is not bounded here.
fields.direction: Re-run the balance for named ground conditions (asphalt apron, hangar wall); measure emissivity of the actual face finish.
fields.effect: The core-limit conclusion could invert on a hot-ground site.

fields.gap: Property loss at temperature is datasheet-class only: H35 derates above 50 to 60 C, SiC is flat far above this range, and the aluminium family derates above about 150 C, not reached. No derate curves are pinned and the daily cycle fatigue of core and adhesive is not quantified.
fields.direction: Pin derate curves for the core and adhesive against the measured daily band; couple to NFI-016-CTE.
fields.effect: The scored five modes use room-temperature properties for a cycling structure.

fields.gap: Face permeation is nil against the 1-percent budget: metals and monolithic SiC are gas barriers; CFRP epoxy laminate passes 5.4e-5 percent of budget on a QUESTIONABLE NASA composite-cryotank helium band divided by 50 for air. No measured air permeance exists for the actual faces.
fields.direction: Measure air permeance of the chosen face and seam coupon directly; matters only if the leak budget is tightened far below 1 percent per day.
fields.effect: None at the current budget; decisive if the budget tightens by four or more orders.

fields.issue: No operating site, measured temperature/pressure/humidity envelope or cold-case minimum is specified. The selected weather cases are assumptions, not site return-period limits.
fields.next_evidence: Replace the declared envelope with station data and operating constraints; recompute both mass and maximum differential-pressure cases.

fields.issue: Zero payload is an unladen demonstrator choice. The former 009c5 payload/margin number cannot simultaneously be mission payload and contingency.
fields.next_evidence: Set payload and remaining float reserve separately. The +100 kg case is supplied.

fields.issue: Whole-hull leakage, trapped core gas, moisture desorption and outgassing have not been measured. The 30-50 kg passive package is a bill-of-mass estimate, not demonstrated vacuum retention.
fields.next_evidence: Measure normalized total gas load through a complete representative panel/valve assembly, then the hull. For the stated 24 h, pstart=10 Pa at T0 and Tint<=320 K, Qref must be <=40.71949 Pa m3/s.

fields.issue: Neither 4 m nor 0.6 m curved thin S200F sandwich panels are established catalog products. The predecessor's 0.6-1.2 m rolled-sheet availability claim lacked a qualifying source. Required 18 m equivalent widths also exceed the local square-panel approximation's useful domain.
fields.next_evidence: Obtain a manufacturer-specific material grade, size, forming route, thickness tolerance and yield quote; replace 2A/w with a spherical seam-layout takeoff.

fields.issue: Two face strips, their bond lines, core splice and full-area face/core adhesive are now counted. Strip sizing and .015/.030 lb/ft2 film use are not qualified for Be, peel, thermal cycling or vacuum; .015 is only a mass lower choice.
fields.next_evidence: Test a complete seam and bond architecture and measure its installed mass, leak rate and stiffness; do not infer that seam-only panel width closes the full joint allowance.

fields.issue: The battery estimate assumes 150 Wh/kg packaged, 80% usable and 90% conversion. Catalog pump speed/power are not installed duty measurements; the smaller SV220B cannot meet the stated hot-gas flow at the fixed pressure cap.
fields.next_evidence: Measure the SV300B or alternative system's curve, input power, cooling, line conductance and duty cycle; procure a qualified power package. Passive and 8 h sensitivities isolate the endurance assumption.

fields.issue: The current Materion forms sheet lists 290 GPa for S200F and 303 GPa for S200FH. Main comparisons deliberately retain the pinned 303 GPa, 283 MPa compression and nu=0.33; the 290 GPa sensitivity is supplied.
fields.next_evidence: Reconcile the exact grade, compression basis, Poisson ratio and sheet/curved-face properties before revising the material point; do not substitute a tensile value for compression.

fields.issue: The inherited Vc=2 rule changes gamma from kd to 1. MAINLINE-018 owns its physical assessment. Under large reserve the aramid optimum leaves the crimp branch, invalidating constant-slope extrapolation.
fields.next_evidence: Resolve the knockdown/branch model and recompute the same margin lines; this card preserves the ordered scoring rule.

fields.issue: SAES explicitly offers room-temperature nitrogen sorption. The unfinished script's blanket denial and unsourced N2 capacity band cannot support its mass result. All-air getter lifetime including noble gases remains unsized.
fields.next_evidence: Use measured species loads, sorption speeds and capacities with activation conditions; do not award a getter-only all-air system a mass credit.

fields.issue: The severe case mathematically selects about 0.056-0.057 mm Be faces and 6.8-8.3 mm core. These are unqualified fabrication and continuum-model geometries; every scored least factor is far below 1.
fields.next_evidence: Treat the result as an estimate of the gap, not a build point; local face/core geometry, buckling imperfections, seam load transfer and nonlinear validation remain open.

fields.issue: Water films are equivalent retained thickness over the whole area, not rainfall depths. Moisture absorbed in core, corrosion, thermal gradients and property derating are not separately quantified here. Gas temperature <=320 K is an acceptance condition, not a thermal prediction.
fields.next_evidence: Measure water shedding, conditioning, absorbed moisture and thermal response for the selected assembly.

fields.issue: This closes the card's explicit budget, not every aircraft subsystem. Separate coating, hardpoint/spreader, mooring attachment, handling, navigation or propulsion masses are not individually sized. The optimistic case retains 70 kg of unused system allowance; the active case has no such spare allowance.
fields.next_evidence: Allocate each needed item explicitly before calling this a complete vehicle mass statement; do not spend retained allowance twice.

fields.issue: The summed margin is consumed at the declared design condition; it is not an additional residual flight contingency or positive safety factor. The cases do not form a statistical confidence interval.
fields.next_evidence: Specify residual operational lift reserve and contingency after the environmental/system charges; add that amount to the budget.

fields.issue: The inherited partial script was not runnable and omitted the 86400 divisor in gas throughput plus the g-to-kg conversion for getter mass. MAINLINE-016 used a linear temperature loss and a constant-final-ratio commissioning expression.
fields.next_evidence: Use this script's normalized throughput, exact p/T climate calculation and variable-pressure reversible integral. Actual ground pump-down energy still needs measurement.

fields.note: 1.5 GPa and 80 um at 970 kg/m3 are the 011b pin. They are not a candidate allowable.
Pillow radius is set to the bay side, 2.04 m, because that is the 011b film formula. It is not a measured cap.
Where no creep-rupture fraction was opened, the design stress is half the opened ultimate. Kapton, Teonex and Vectran use it.

fields.state: exists as a filament test note
fields.note: The 19 year life is Toyobo's extrapolation of an HM filament at 60 percent of break, not a laminate test.
A uniaxial filament needs a 0/90 build to carry both pillow directions. Total thickness is twice the one-direction thickness. No resin is included, so a real laminate is heavier.
The 20 percent fraction and the 15 and 250 year lives are indicative rope numbers at 16 C, not a film.
Density is the printed GPa divided by the printed N/tex. The sheet does not print density.
The design thickness is above the 250 um row. The 210 MPa ultimate is the thickest opened gauge, not a measurement at the design thickness.
The IEC Teonex sheet says its typical values are not design data.
The barrier brochure has no PET strength, modulus, density or creep. The 12 um mass is not computed.
The oxygen column does not print the test pressure. The scale uses 1 atm of oxygen.
N2 is opened for Kapton only. PEN, Mylar and the ALD paper do not give N2.
The case has no exterior humidity. Water loads stay at the sheet condition and are not a hull rate.
The alumina numbers are coupon measurements. A 1257 m2 hull coating was not opened. Tagged PROJECTION at hull scale.
No getter capacity is stated. The pump band is the 150 to 400 kg catalog class, not scaled to the gas load.
No production allowable was opened. Thickness is not stated.
A filament crossply is not taken as gas-tight. The barrier is a separate layer.
Dry-air mole fractions 0.20946 and 0.78084 are not in the vacuum case.

fields.issue: The large 020 panel is 0.6096×1.8288 m; its quoted stock maximum begins at 0.059 in (1.4986 mm). At R = 20 the enhanced aluminium face is only 1.423 mm. The conservative small panel is an assumed 0.3048×0.6096 m. Some severe-budget faces are far below the supplier's stated sheet gauge.
fields.next_evidence: Supplier-confirm panel dimensions at each minimum gauge, shaping yield, thickness distribution and installed geometry; re-run with procurement bounds.

fields.issue: Frozen 020 kg/m 2 hides Be-doubler and core-gap masses that grow with optimized thickness. The corrected model holds widths/gaps fixed but resizes their depths. Neither seam is mechanically designed.
fields.next_evidence: Weigh and load-test a curved two-skin splice; establish widths, gaps, taper, sealing, peel, fatigue and stiffness as functions of face/core thickness.

fields.issue: 020's 0.9/0.6 net-section efficiencies are assumed screens, applied only to compression. The enhanced aluminium optimum is global/joint limited. No joint buckling, shear or peel allowables exist.
fields.next_evidence: Measure the seam's biaxial compression, load eccentricity and failure envelope; do not count straps as structural stiffness without a model.

fields.issue: Design uses the inherited hemispherical 0.2/1 step at Vc=2. Full 021 uses 0.2+0.4min(Vc,2). Neither is validated for this completed sphere. Constant 0.2 removes the enhanced P2 pass.
fields.next_evidence: Carry the 018b and 015 evidence into an installed-geometry shell test/model, retaining imperfection maps.

fields.issue: S-200F E = 290 GPa and inherited compression 283 MPa are the design screen. Full 021 transfers a historical SR-200 lot's 379.2 MPa and lower in-plane E = 293.6 GPa. Current SR-200 sheet lists E = 290 GPa and tensile minimum 345 MPa, not a guaranteed compression allowable. Nu 0.33 remains inherited.
fields.next_evidence: Obtain lot-, gauge-, direction- and post-form compression/stiffness/Poisson data. Keep these mechanical optimism choices separate from weather optimism.

fields.issue: 5056 3/8-1.0 uses the published typical Ec/Gc/crush row; stabilized modulus is used in the wrinkle formula. Manufacturer tests were at 15.875 mm depth; optimized cores reach roughly 120–144 mm at R = 50.
fields.next_evidence: Validate thick curved honeycomb, skin restraint, orthotropy, cell-depth effects, local modes, thermal response and crush definition. Catalogue sensitivity includes Plascore rows with Ec transferred from Hexcel and bare compression substituted for crush.

fields.issue: One SV300B catalog pumping speed is insufficient for 019's volume-proportional 1%/day gas load above R = 10. Modular counting gives 1,3,7,23,103 pumps at 10,15,20,30,50 m, with full rated power continuously budgeted. Installed conductance/manifolds are not sized.
fields.next_evidence: Measure leak/outgas and installed speed at pressure; replace the assumed gas-load law and duty cycle with a measured area/seam/volume decomposition.

fields.issue: The 30 kg sealed-service package is held fixed. Its normalized gas-load limit grows with volume; this does not prove its seals, plumbing, monitoring or ground evacuation hardware scale at fixed mass.
fields.next_evidence: Demonstrate 24 h hold at the temperature envelope, seal transients, pressure monitoring and ground-service capability; add supporting hardware mass.

fields.issue: The optimistic +10 K/±1%/1000 Pa vapour and conservative +25.1 K/±2%/6000 Pa cases are owner scenarios, not a site distribution. Water is a full-area equivalent retained film, contamination an area load.
fields.next_evidence: Specify site, gas composition, temperatures, weather exposure, water shedding/icing and mission duration; retain both low-density lift and high-pressure strength envelopes.

fields.issue: Extra coatings, lightning protection, mooring, hardpoints, navigation and propulsion are not independently sized. P2 retains a 100 kg system floor, including 70 kg above the passive package, but this is not a complete vehicle mass model.
fields.next_evidence: Itemize additional vehicle masses. An extra 0.1 kg/m 2 is included as a P2 sensitivity; 209.84 kg payload at R = 20 is only 41.75 g/m 2 of additional areal mass.

fields.issue: Diameters grow 20→100 m, projected ground area and wind force at fixed speed grow 25-fold, characteristic overturning moment 125-fold. Point attachments, transport, launch and landing are outside uniform-pressure modes.
fields.next_evidence: Design and weigh handling/anchoring/assembly equipment and verify concentrated and asymmetric loads, gust response and damage tolerance.

fields.issue: P3 asks for metre-scale curved, thin-walled SiC tubes and a pressure membrane at 1.5 GPa allowable. The opened supplier seal-tube example is typically 12 in long. These components and their formed geometry are not demonstrated products.
fields.next_evidence: Establish tube/film manufacturing, joints, porosity/leaks, defects, proof loads and installation tolerances; then replace bounds with physical ones.

fields.issue: 011b's SiC compression 3900 MPa and metal-style Perry interaction produce the P3 pass. A380 MPa strength screen gives only about 0.24–0.25 over 10–50 m. Compressive strength is not a ceramic bending/tensile allowable.
fields.next_evidence: Use a brittle tension/compression interaction, statistical size effect and joint eccentricity rather than certifying on the inherited Perry score.

fields.issue: P3 retains 20 g/node and 5% tube-mass joints without measured capacity or complete film-attachment masses. A load-linked node-mass sensitivity changes little numerically, but does not validate the 20 g anchor.
fields.next_evidence: Size nodes and film attachment/seams from load paths. Same topology with truly similar solid nodes would make each node's mass scale as R^3.

fields.issue: P3 reoptimization holds bay 0.4–3 m and radius≤0.25 m. The radius cap governs large hulls. Similarity rows separately scale members but hold 80 µm film, making film SF fall as 1/R.
fields.next_evidence: Treat relaxed member caps or thicker film as separately costed designs; do not infer a universal radius optimum from this bounded continuation.

fields.issue: Reserve is the explicit charge above retained baseline system/joint floors, not statistical contingency or free payload. Climate plus internal air alone is 5.7396% optimistic and 13.1183% conservative.
fields.next_evidence: If a sub 5% requirement is mandatory, change/justify the climate or gas assumptions or definition. Increasing radius alone cannot meet it.

fields.issue: The dispatch names a nonmatching 019 report ID; actual verified ID uses lead-sci. Original 021 hashes are superseded by revision 1, which was used. Scientific uncertainty remains despite arithmetic checks.
fields.next_evidence: Use INPUTS.json's 53 verified/measured pins and the actual 019/revised 021 filing IDs; freeze this card after filing.

fields.row: S-200F headline and SR-200 gamma-only sensitivity
fields.tag: QUESTIONABLE sourced typical, not a guaranteed minimum

fields.already_known: The owner was ordered to correct E at 00:21:45; the observed changed results use E290 and a separate SR-200 modulus. This check does not certify that later packet.

fields.tag: QUESTIONABLE transfer from an orthotropic 1.96-mm sheet lot; not a replacement isotropic specification
fields.disposition: Arithmetic follows the pinned nu=.33. Treat that as an explicit inherited assumption, not a sourced beryllium property. The demonstrated sensitivity changes the preferred two-optimism set.
fields.proposed_fix: A card using a coherent measured in-plane elastic tuple and an appropriate orthotropic model, or an explicitly tagged isotropic approximation.

fields.row: No strength optimism / sheet at guaranteed minimum
fields.effect: No strength optimism is true only relative to the inherited 283-MPa starting value. The current guide's S-200F value does not support that point without an uplift. The 345-MPa sheet number is tensile; equality in compression is an additional transfer assumption.
fields.product_form: The S-200F datasheet offers SR-200 sheet and PS-200 foil as additional options below 6.3 mm; it does not establish an exclusive mandatory substitution. SR-200 below 0.059 inch is available only at smaller sheet dimensions. The datasheet's parenthetic 0.059 inch = 0.5 mm is internally inconsistent (0.059 inch = 1.4986 mm).
fields.disposition: Confirms and sharpens the owner's existing Be-strength/sheet-size NFI; does not stop the estimate.
fields.proposed_fix: Use a matched product/lot/thickness compression value; keep the tensile-to-compressive transfer explicit. MAINLINE-020 is the named grounding card.

fields.location: CR-194164 Table 3; TN D-4833 Table VIII, PDF page 35
fields.effect: 379.2 MPa is supported for the cited sheet directions, but is not the largest compressive value in the source collection. The larger numbers are tube results, not qualified sphere faces.
fields.proposed_fix: Narrow the wording to strongest applicable sheet value among the opened sheet sources. A tube-to-sheet transfer, if pursued, is a separate PROJECTION.

fields.gap: All buckling requirements use kd = 0.2 and scale as 1/kd. MAINLINE-004's named knockdown curve is still running.
fields.direction: Multiply each E requirement by 0.2/kd when 004 lands; no other number changes.
fields.effect: A larger knockdown factor lowers every required E in this card.

fields.gap: 276 MPa is a QUESTIONABLE typical tensile yield transferred to compression (inherited NFI-AL-YIELD-CARRY). Required strengths here are membrane stresses and do not depend on it; only the x276 MPa multiples and SF labels do.
fields.direction: Obtain a compressive design allowable and rescale the multiples only.
fields.effect: No required Pa value in this card moves.

fields.gap: P2 equal-mass figure holds face separation at the row value while face thickness follows 1/rho. A changed face density moves tf and so moves separation by the same amount, a second-order change against 0.1-0.16 m cores.
fields.direction: Recompute E/rho with separation following tf if a candidate face material is far from 2700 kg/m3.
fields.effect: Small optimistic or pessimistic shift in the P2 buckling figure for extreme densities.

fields.gap: P3 figures use thin-wall A and I at fixed outer radius. P3-A has tw/ro = 0.175, where thin-wall understates I for a given mass.
fields.direction: Use exact annulus A and I for a named candidate section.
fields.effect: P3-A's E/rho requirement is mildly pessimistic; exact section helps it.

fields.gap: Film allowable 1.5 GPa is inherited from MAINLINE-001 with no pinned datasheet (inherited NFI-FILM). The film passes at SF 2.51 on that value.
fields.direction: Pin one film datasheet; required allowable 5.966e8 Pa is the bar it must clear.
fields.effect: A real film below 5.966e8 Pa allowable would govern P3 and P3-A.

fields.gap: Core shear, face wrinkling, core crush, local crippling and end fixity remain outside these two limits, as in 002/003. Core crush is worked next as MAINLINE-005b.
fields.direction: 005b for crush; later cards for shear, wrinkling and crippling.
fields.effect: Any omitted mode can only lower a row's true SF below the figures here.

fields.gap: The p/2 core stress is the brief's example model, QUESTIONABLE, with no pinned sandwich reference. Local face bending and load spreading are ignored.
fields.direction: Pin a sandwich core-crush reference and re-derive the factor.
fields.effect: Required core strength scales linearly with whatever factor replaces 1/2.

fields.gap: Foam strengths are quoted at 1% and 10% strain by different sources. The incumbent 16 kg/m3 passes on one definition and fails on the other.
fields.direction: The checker names the governing strain definition for a vacuum shell core.
fields.effect: Lowest passing density moves between about 11 and about 22 kg/m3 on that choice.

fields.gap: MAINLINE-007 is not filed yet, so its rows have no crush numbers here, only the ready formula.
fields.direction: Apply p/2 at 007's external pressure when that card lands.
fields.effect: None until 007 exists.

fields.gap: EPS at 10% strain is a short-term value; sustained vacuum loading creeps. No creep derate is applied.
fields.direction: Derate foam allowables for sustained load before any density near 11 kg/m3 is relied on.
fields.effect: The practical lowest density is higher than 11 kg/m3.

fields.issue: QI laminate E and compressive strength for T700, M55J, K13D2U and boron/epoxy are estimates from UD/fibre data with the stated reduction factors, not measured laminate cards.
fields.effect: Those four rows move with the assumed QI factors; fibre properties were not used, per the brief.
fields.needed: Measured QI laminate modulus and compressive strength for each system at the intended fibre volume fraction.

fields.issue: 6061-T6, 7075-T6, 2195-T8 and AlBeMet 162 compressive strengths are tensile yields transferred to compression; AZ31 uses a compressive yield, Ti-6Al-4V and Be S-200F use compressive values, SiC a compressive ultimate, Vitreloy 1 a compressive ultimate.
fields.effect: SF_y for transferred rows is QUESTIONABLE; the 6061 baseline itself is the pinned transfer, so ratios are consistent with 002/003.
fields.needed: Measured compressive yield for each metal temper and product form.

fields.issue: SiC and beryllium rank on compressive membrane modes only. SiC flexural strength (~380 MPa) and fracture toughness, and beryllium toxicity, joining and low ductility, are outside both formulas.
fields.effect: A high least-SF here is not a buildable face; bending, impact, attachment and thermal paths can govern.
fields.needed: A fracture/joining assessment before either is carried as a face material.

fields.issue: Core shear, face wrinkling, core crush, laminate anisotropy (nu, shear), face-core bond and thermal stress are omitted, as in 002/003; equal face mass holds the pinned core and separation fixed.
fields.effect: SF_b is a first-order tf<<d scaling; a candidate whose tf approached d, or whose nu differs strongly, would need the full sandwich formulas.
fields.needed: MAINLINE-004 knockdown for kd rescaling, and a sandwich failure check per candidate.

fields.issue: CNT-yarn and graphene QI rows are PROJECTION scenarios, not available materials; their assumed values are stated per row.
fields.effect: They bound a direction, not a procurement option; the available-only best three are listed separately.
fields.needed: A demonstrated QI CNT-yarn or graphene laminate card.

fields.issue: All buckling SFs inherit kd=0.2; required E scales as 1/kd (Una's 003 correction), so every SF_b scales linearly with kd/0.2.
fields.effect: MAINLINE-004's knockdown rescales every buckling column by one multiplication, as COMMON.md states.
fields.needed: MAINLINE-004 filed values (next job 008c).

fields.issue: The re-rank rows at 4 and 1 kg/m3 presume a structural core that does not exist today. MAINLINE-007 retrieved no catalog core with sourced shear modulus, compressive modulus and strength below 16 kg/m3 (Plascore lightest 16, ROHACELL IG-F starts 31, HexWeb lightest retrieved 24; Schaedler nickel microlattice 0.9 kg/m3 has no retrieved modulus or strength).
fields.consequence: Every light-core row in this card is PROJECTION on the core side regardless of face material. The wrinkling comparison on those rows uses Ec*Gc products belonging to 24-38 kg/m3 cores, which cannot ride on a 1-4 kg/m3 row at any thickness near the mass ceiling (a 32 kg/m3 core at the 1 kg/m3 row's 0.1884 m thickness would alone mass about 7576 kg against a 4889 kg ceiling).
fields.next: Source or project an ultra-light core with a stated Ec*Gc product and strength; until then the light-core readings measure the core gap, not a build.

fields.issue: The wrinkling criterion sigma_wr = 0.5*(E_f*Ec*Gc)^(1/3) is the flat-panel/dimple formula transferred to a 10 m radius sandwich sphere. Orthotropic honeycomb has no single continuum Ec; the two HexWeb sheets carry no compressive modulus on their datasheets, so their Ec*Gc products stay open (007). Foam products (ROHACELL, Divinycell) are datasheet-derived and QUESTIONABLE.
fields.consequence: The wrinkling column measures a product gap, not a verified failure mode. MAINLINE-007b is sourced to replace this reading.
fields.next: 007b's sourced sandwich-shell shear and wrinkling formulas supersede this column when filed.

fields.issue: The quasi-isotropic moduli 54, 135, 210, 86 and 180 GPa are rounded products of their stated bases (53.6, 136.5, 211.15, 85.68, 179.2); the unidirectional compressive strengths behind 520, 350 and 220 MPa are unnamed.
fields.consequence: Recomputing with the unrounded products does not change any rank order in this card (verified for P2-E by the checker; the light-core rows scale all candidates by the same ratios, so their order is unchanged too).
fields.next: Write each QI modulus as its product and name the UD strengths when the material set is next touched.

fields.issue: At equal face mass the face-thickness change moves the separation slightly; the first-order scaling drops that term. The 008 checker measured the effect at most 0.348 percent of SF_b on P2-E (worst tf/d 0.00722).
fields.consequence: Negligible against the 2-10x gaps this card reports.
fields.next: None alone; folds into any future exact recompute.

fields.issue: The P3 columns use the thin-wall tube figures; the approximation is weakest on P3-A where tw/ro = 0.175.
fields.consequence: P3 rows are order-of-magnitude readings; nothing in P3 passes anyway.
fields.next: None unless a candidate family approaches P3 feasibility.

fields.issue: The conservative SP-8032 factor is a monocoque cap curve transferred to the sandwich (phi = pi, t_eq = (6 tf d^2)^(1/3)); the central 0.20 is monocoque dome evidence; the 0.90 carry is from shells at lambda 1.58-33.18 while this sphere sits near lambda 65-68.
fields.consequence: All three levels are QUESTIONABLE; the optimistic 0.90 is outside the regime by 004b's own reading.
fields.next: 007b-adjacent: a sandwich-specific knockdown for this geometry.

fields.gap: Levers 1 and 4 hold face and core thickness fixed while radius changes. A real design re-optimizes thickness per radius; the mass-ceiling rows of 002/003 show how much that moves things at 10 m only.
fields.direction: Re-run the levers with thickness re-solved at the float ceiling per radius.
fields.effect: Margins improve at small radius; SF rankings are not expected to flip.

fields.gap: Systems at 100 kg per sphere in a cluster is the mass rule read literally. A shared-systems cluster would pay it once.
fields.direction: Name the systems architecture before crediting any cluster margin.
fields.effect: Cluster margins improve by up to (n-1) x 100 kg of lift; SFs unchanged.

fields.gap: ISA is a standard column, not weather. The 500 m point matches the pinned case within 0.1 Pa; other altitudes are the same formula, QUESTIONABLE.
fields.direction: Fly a measured column when a site is named.
fields.effect: Lever 2 numbers move with the real lapse and pressure.

fields.gap: MAINLINE-007 and 008 had not filed when this card closed, so lever 1 was not re-run on their best rows, as the brief's Then clause directs.
fields.direction: Re-run lever 1 on their best rows when they file; the script here takes any tf/core row.
fields.effect: None on this card's numbers.

fields.gap: No global frame mode: the model checks member Euler, member yield, tube local buckling and film only. Snap-through or general-instability of the whole stiffened sphere between nodes is unmodelled, and MAINLINE-004's spherical knockdown therefore neither applies to nor rescales any P3 number.
fields.direction: Add an equivalent-stiffened-shell general-instability check (ribbed-sphere analogy) before any P3 number is read as a whole-vehicle figure.
fields.effect: Could only lower the P3 rows; the aluminum plateau's flatness and the material ranking survive any such factor applied uniformly.

fields.gap: The unconstrained optimum rides the node-mass saving to s=6.4 m (V=37 nodes), where the equal-triangle continuum behind V(s) is no longer a defensible reading; the reported optimum is cut at s<=3.0 m (V>=161), suppressing 0.0002 of SF.
fields.direction: Re-run on real geodesic layouts (unequal members, real tributary areas) if a design point is ever picked.
fields.effect: At most +0.1 percent on aluminum; no ranking change.

fields.gap: sigma_local = 0.6*E*t_w/r_o is SP-8007 classical with gamma=1 (no imperfection knockdown). At the aluminum best, local sits 3.9x above the least SF, so the answer is robust; at the T700 best the margin is 1.18x, and a gamma of 0.65 would pull that point's local to ~0.59.
fields.direction: Re-optimise r_o under a knocked-down local curve: at s=1 the local margin is 2.6x, so the material conclusion (T700 least ~0.76, yield-bound) survives down to gamma ~0.29 after re-optimisation.
fields.effect: The best-point geometry moves; the least SF per material does not.

fields.gap: SiC's 3900 MPa is a crushing value; 008's own NFI carries that flexural ~380 MPa governs any bending or tension path, with brittle fracture, joining and handling unresolved. A 0.04 m radius sintered SiC tube of 1.3 mm wall is undemonstrated.
fields.direction: Treat the SiC row as a material-boundary statement (sigma/rho headroom), not a buildable tube.
fields.effect: The P3 sigma/rho-bound conclusion stands; the SiC design point does not.

fields.gap: The film allowable 1.5e9 Pa is an owner assumption with no datasheet, and wrinkling, puncture, sag area and shear transfer to members are unmodelled. For aluminum the film never binds (>=0.838 at the best point), but for SiC and the CNT projection it is the second limit and binds from s=1.0.
fields.direction: Pin a real film (material, thickness, seaming) before crediting any SiC-family margin.
fields.effect: SiC-family rows are film-capped in reality until the film is real.

fields.gap: Node count is the equilateral-continuum formula (equal members, equal tributary area R*s per member, load N=p*R*s/2 — the 002 pinned load path), node hardware 0.02 kg each, and no separate joint or gusset mass exists for P3 in the pinned mass rules.
fields.direction: Real geodesic load paths and joint masses before any design pick.
fields.effect: Node and joint mass growth eats tube mass one-for-one at the ceiling; SF_yield falls in proportion.

fields.gap: NFI-005-THINWALL answered: all sections here are exact annuli, and at every reported optimum t_w/r_o lies in 0.019-0.076 (thin). Only the 005-frame comparison rows at fixed r_o=0.02 sit thick (t_w/r_o 0.175 aluminum, up to 0.38 for swaps), where the thin-cylinder local formula itself is weakest.
fields.direction: None for this card's optima; the 005-frame rows are comparison only.
fields.effect: None on the reported optima.

fields.issue: No measured core at or below 10 kg/m3 meets the wrinkling need with 6061 faces on the P2 float ceiling.
fields.numbers: Best measured: meza2014-hollow-alumina-octet-lightest-E at 5.5 kg/m3, Ec*Gc margin 0.000171 on the least-factor split (gap 5.84e+03, 18 on stress; 1.66e+03 at the classical 0.76), gap 1.7e+04 on the buckling split. Band 1-4 kg/m3: kashani2019-npg-3-tension, gap 7.57e+04 (2.16e+04 classical).
fields.closes_when: a measured core's Ec*Gc at its own density meets the need on its row; or a face change lowers the need, which scales as sigma_face^3/E_face (008b's face table); or a wrinkling test on a representative sandwich replaces the CR-1457 design coefficient.

fields.issue: No source measured a transverse shear modulus for any core at or below 10 kg/m3.
fields.numbers: Gc is DERIVED as Ec/2 (isotropic, nu = 0, the optimistic bound) for every non-honeycomb core; at nu = 1/3 every product falls by 0.75 and every crimp margin by 0.75. Si et al. 2014 measured shear stress at 9.6 kg/m3 but printed no modulus.
fields.closes_when: a plate-shear or sandwich-beam shear modulus is measured on a candidate core.

fields.issue: On the least-factor split no measured core at or below 10 kg/m3 reaches the crimp shear modulus.
fields.numbers: Need 2.52e+06 Pa at 1 to 9.6 kg/m3; best meza2014-hollow-alumina-octet-lightest-E margin 0.735 (gap 1.36) on the derived Gc. On the buckling split three alumina lattice points pass (0.3, 5.3, 5.5 kg/m3), the 0.3 point on a 6 m core.
fields.closes_when: a measured Gc above the need on the row the design uses.

fields.issue: Most ultralight strengths are not crush strengths: stress at 80 percent strain (Qiu 2012), undefined 'max stress' (Si 2014), ultimate stress of undefined strain (Xu 2019), 40 percent compression (Basotect), indentation or tension (Kashani 2019). These can fail the crush check but never pass it.
fields.numbers: The only structural pass at or below 10 kg/m3 is meza2015-hier-hollow-alumina-heaviest-halfcell at 5.3 kg/m3, margin 1.34, read by eye from a plot (about 25 percent) with its density inferred from relative density times 2900 kg/m3.
fields.closes_when: a small-strain collapse or yield strength is measured at the candidate density.

fields.issue: This card sourced no core between 53 and 190 kg/m3, so the lightest core passing all three is bounded, not found.
fields.numbers: The only pass is jacobsen2011-vitreous-carbon-octet-0p19 at 190 kg/m3 (secondary source); at that density the float-ceiling core is 9.2 mm thick and the shell's buckling SF is 0.0204 at kd 0.2.
fields.closes_when: mid-density cores are sourced (for example high-density PMI foams, end-grain balsa, carbon micro-lattices from 50 to 190 kg/m3) and run through compute.py.

fields.issue: Two values arrive second-hand: the vitreous carbon octet micro-lattice (Jacobsen 2011, via Zhang 2019) and the glassy carbon exponents (Bauer 2016, via Zhang 2019); Schaedler 2011's 10 kg/m3 nickel point also via Zhang 2019.
fields.numbers: The 190 kg/m3 all-three pass rests on the secondary Jacobsen numbers (1.1 GPa, 10.2 MPa).
fields.closes_when: the primary papers are opened and the values matched.

fields.issue: Maloney 2013, Zheng 2016, Meza 2014, Meza 2015 and Zhu 2015 values are read by eye from log plots (about 25 to 50 percent); the Meza densities are inferred from relative density.
fields.numbers: None of these readings sits near a margin of 1 except the Meza 2015 crush point (1.34).
fields.closes_when: tabulated values (journal SI or theses) replace the readings.

fields.issue: The continuum wrinkling form assumes a core finer than the wrinkle wavelength; lattice cell sizes were not sourced. Intracell dimpling, a fourth local mode outside the card's three, is reported beside them.
fields.numbers: CR-1457 eq 2.1-4 with the straight-line biaxial rule allows cells up to 3.52 mm above 9.6 kg/m3 and up to 9.84 mm on the least-factor split at 0.1 kg/m3; every honeycomb cell in the table fails it except the 1/8-inch (1.11).
fields.closes_when: cell sizes are sourced and a wrinkling model valid at that cell scale is applied.

fields.issue: CR-1457 eq 2.2-14 at these core-to-face ratios (tc/tf about 220 to 560) is far outside its test data; it makes the honeycomb need an Ec no honeycomb has.
fields.numbers: Ec needed 1.03e+10 to 7.74e+10 Pa; best honeycomb margin 0.00462 (gap 216).
fields.closes_when: a symmetric-wrinkling model or test for very thick honeycomb cores, or a honeycomb with a stabilising foam fill.

fields.issue: The 6061 face is past its QUESTIONABLE 276 MPa on every row, so the elastic wrinkling forms (eta 1) flatter it.
fields.numbers: Face stress 3.57e+08 Pa (Q, 0.1 kg/m3) to 7.09e+08 Pa.
fields.closes_when: the face material changes (008b) or CR-1457 section 9 plasticity factors are applied.

fields.issue: On the buckling split the core exceeds a tenth of the radius below about 1.8 kg/m3 and the radius itself below about 0.18 kg/m3, so B-split margins there are not physical (external-area and thin-shell rules).
fields.numbers: B core 1.81 m at 1 kg/m3, 18.1 m at 0.1 kg/m3; the Q split holds h = 0.18907 m and is valid at every density.
fields.closes_when: a thick-shell sandwich model with the inner surface area replaces the external-area rule.

fields.issue: The ideal stretch-dominated lattice (Ashby 2006 eq 5.1, Gc = Ec/2) is a bound, not a material; strength is not projected because no strut-buckling constant was sourced.
fields.numbers: Passes wrinkling and crimp on the least-factor split from 1.34 (K13D2U-grade), 2.46 (CNT yarn), 4.82 (beryllium), 25.3 (alumina), 55.9 kg/m3 (6061). At 5 kg/m3 a lattice needs 0.378, 0.628 and 0.982 of ideal; measured alumina lattices reach 0.0279 to 0.0422.
fields.closes_when: a lattice of a fibre-grade strut material is built and measured at 1 to 8 kg/m3.

fields.issue: The wrinkling-precision gap, carried as 009 and 014 carry it: design coefficients (continuum 0.50, CR-1457 eq 2.2-5; honeycomb 0.33, eq 2.2-14) against classical ones (0.76, NASA/CR-1999-208994 Table 3; 0.82, eq 2.2-12).
fields.numbers: The product need falls to 0.285 at 0.76 (a factor 3.51); the honeycomb Ec need falls to 0.162 at 0.82 (6.17). No verdict in this card moves.
fields.closes_when: a representative wrinkling test fixes the coefficient for the chosen face and core.

fields.issue: The p/2 core-stress model is the brief's own example, QUESTIONABLE; local face bending is ignored.
fields.numbers: Required 47730.4 Pa on every row.
fields.closes_when: a sandwich-sphere through-thickness solution replaces it.

fields.issue: EPS strengths are specification minima at 1, 5 or 10 percent strain, and the sheets disagree.
fields.numbers: EPS12 (11.2 kg/m3): 15 kPa at 1 percent and 40 kPa at 10 percent (ASTM D6817 minima, margins 0.314 and 0.838); 34 kPa at 10 percent (older C578 minimum, 0.712); 005b's National Polystyrene 50 kPa at 11 kg/m3 gave 1.05.
fields.closes_when: the design adopts one strain definition and a measured (not minimum) value.

fields.issue: Every lattice and aerogel in this table was tested as a laboratory specimen (micrometres to centimetres); the float-ceiling core is about 1257 m2 by 0.19 m. The commercial foams (EPS, melamine, polyimide) are made at larger scale but fail the checks by orders of magnitude. Vacuum outgassing, creep under a sustained p/2 (polymer foams), and temperature were not assessed.
fields.numbers: No lattice or aerogel source here reports a manufacturing route at metre scale.
fields.closes_when: a manufacturing route at metre scale is sourced for a candidate core.

fields.issue: Sources that were paywalled or blocked, so none of their values is used: Schaedler 2011 full text and SI, Torrents 2012, Valdevit 2013, Salari-Sharif 2014, Zheng 2014 (Science 344, 1373), Jang 2013, Deshpande-Ashby-Fleck 2001, Gross and Fricke 1995, Woignier 1989 full text, Ma 2000 full text, Sun 2013, Hu 2013, Zou 2010, Gui 2010, Worsley 2009 and 2012, Mecklenburg 2012, Eckel 2016, Bauer 2016, Jacobsen 2011.
fields.numbers: Zheng 2014 (MIT DSpace HTTP 429, Science 403) is the likeliest source of a stiffer ultralight ceramic octet point.
fields.closes_when: those texts are obtained and their values added through build_cores.py.

fields.issue: Eq 3 floors at 0.45, so kd 0.3 has no lambda_I = 1 amplitude. The worst-width curve is pinned only at its plateau 0.2338 and by the one-thickness statement, kd about 0.20-0.25 at delta equal to t. kd 0.3 sits on the unretrieved rising branch between those pins. No pair is interpolated. The aluminium-honeycomb beryllium point has R/t_eq 136.7, inside the fit range 100-1550, so the missing amplitude is the floor, not the range. P2-E at R/t_eq 50.75 remains outside that range.
fields.consequence: The kd 0.3 row is a ceiling: below 197.052 mm on P2-E, below 73.17 mm on the 014b beryllium point, below 39.05 mm on 014 beryllium with HRH-10. The true allowance is smaller, and the gap factor against manufacture is not known.
fields.next: Digitise the worst-width envelope (Lee et al. 2016, or a recomputation) at delta/t below 1.

fields.issue: The 014b beryllium point on CR-III 5056 at 1.6 pcf has least SF 0.668649769508548 by global buckling at kd 0.20. Face wrinkling on that same split is 0.6688 and does not contain kd. Raising kd to 0.2991 brings only the global mode to SF 1. The least factor stays 0.6688. Re-optimising the mass split on the same core and the same structural mass reaches least SF 0.8536 at kd 0.3 and crosses 1 at kd 0.519 by face yield.
fields.consequence: A shape tolerance bought at kd 0.3 does not put this point's least factor at 1. The global-only scaling is the order's 0.299, and it is not the least factor.
fields.next: If a later card chases SF 1 on this core, use the re-optimised split and kd 0.519, not the frozen split at kd 0.3.

fields.issue: The gap factor is required tolerance divided by the achieved figure. Above 1, manufacture is already inside the allowance. The partial's sentence that kd 0.9 needs 1.8 times better than the GBT assembled surface reads the P2-E factor 1.82 the other way. On P2-E the 0.46 mm RMS allowance is looser than 0.25 mm. On the aluminium beryllium point the 0.10 mm RMS allowance is tighter than 0.25 mm and looser than 0.05 mm.
fields.consequence: The shell that the kd 0.3 question is about is not free at kd 0.9 on a single-dimple RMS basis, even though P2-E is.
fields.next: None. The arithmetic is in RESULTS.json.

fields.issue: The partial's prose says the gyration thickness and the bending thickness give classical pressures 3.42 times apart. On P2-E, Zoelly's pressure at t_eq divided by the COMMON sandwich pressure is 293.1. The 3.42 figure is not that ratio.
fields.consequence: Safety factors stay on the sandwich pressure. t_eq is used only to scale the dimple.
fields.next: None.

fields.issue: The kd-versus-amplitude relation is closed-form only at width lambda_I = 1. The worst-width curve is pinned at its plateau 0.2338 and by the one-thickness statement. Amplitudes at kd 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9 are lambda_I = 1 values. Worst-width amplitudes at those levels are smaller.
fields.consequence: The inverted table is optimistic in width. The kd 0.2 row is the conservative anchor.
fields.next: Retrieve the min-over-width envelope.

fields.issue: Every kd curve used here is a monocoque result transferred through t_eq = sqrt(3)(d+tf). No sandwich kd-versus-amplitude measurement was retrieved at this radius. The mapping preserves the radius of gyration by construction.
fields.consequence: The tolerance table carries this transfer as its central QUESTIONABLE. It is the sibling of 004b's NFI-KD-TRANSFER.
fields.next: A sandwich imperfection study at this geometry.

fields.issue: Eq 3 was fit over R/t 100-1550 and nu near 0.5. P2-E sits at R/t_eq 50.75 with nu 0.33. The aluminium beryllium point sits at 136.7 and is inside the R/t window. The Poisson mismatch remains on both.
fields.consequence: P2-E amplitudes carry an unquantified range-floor error. The aluminium point does not carry that particular error.
fields.next: A fit at R/t near 50 if P2-E stays the reference shell.

fields.issue: Hutchinson and Thompson 2018 Eq 3.2, the lower envelope over dimple width, was not resolved from the primary. It is not used. The rising branch is Baizhikova 2026 Eq 3, which meets Jimenez at the shared plateau (0.4470 against 0.45).
fields.consequence: No number in this card comes from that unresolved print.
fields.next: Resolve the print against the primary when it can be read.

fields.issue: Core shear's cut to the classical pressure is derived: 10.3, 7.0 and 0.8 percent on P2-E at 9, 14 and 138 MPa, and 11.4 percent on the aluminium core at 72.4 MPa. The cut to imperfection sensitivity has no retrieved coefficient.
fields.consequence: The kd levels are applied with no shear-dependent correction.
fields.next: A shear-flexible imperfection study.

fields.issue: The thickness sensitivity is derived. A locally 10 percent thin face costs 10.0 percent of P2-E classical pressure. No sourced cure tolerance for the faces or the core was retrieved.
fields.consequence: The driver is a sensitivity, not a gap factor.
fields.next: Source autoclave and core-machining tolerances when the build is chosen.

fields.issue: A seam step is counted only as delta/t_eq. A real seam also breaks face continuity. On P2-E the geometric reading is kd 0.950, 0.931 and 0.869 at steps of 1, 3 and 10 mm.
fields.consequence: The geometric reading is not a joint failure mode.
fields.next: A joint model belongs with the sandwich failure cards.

fields.issue: The PNAS 2024 random-field design values are evaluated at R/t_eq 50.75 by scaling N with sqrt(R/t). Their fits span R/t 100-400. The reproduced anchors are 0.278 and 0.320 at R/t 100.
fields.consequence: The P2-E readings are a cross-check, not a design number.
fields.next: Recompute the chain at R/t 50 if that route is carried.

fields.issue: Full-sphere curves are used. A clamped equator can cap kappa near 0.8 for a small dimple. The static hydrostatic column is 240 Pa, 0.25 percent of the case pressure. Pump-down transients are not modelled.
fields.consequence: The high-kd rows assume a complete sphere under uniform quasi-static pressure.
fields.next: An equator, if the design keeps one, needs its own card.

fields.claim: Installed bond/seam mass and capacity are not contained by an evidenced 5% allowance.
fields.needed_to_ground: Ground first: weigh and load a representative curved two-skin/core seam with the intended film coverage, seal, manufacturing defects and post-thermal-cycle condition. Establish seam buckling, shear/peel and leak behavior.
fields.effect_on_lead: The optimistic selected joint already consumes more than the payload; redesign or a much lighter demonstrated joint is needed. Cases are not bounding tests.

fields.claim: Maximum currently purchasable 0.75-0.79 mm panel size and installed shape are UNKNOWN.
fields.needed_to_ground: Ground second, with material NFI: obtain a supplier-confirmed grade/gauge/size/flatness specification, formed-panel gauge map and curvature survey. Measure edge and joint steps; establish trim yield.
fields.effect_on_lead: Thinner-size maximum is unspecified. Uniform upper tolerance adds 472.40 kg faces; low-gauge wrinkle SF is 0.52323. Flatness measured restrained cannot qualify assembled buckling.

fields.claim: S200F bulk properties are not an established rolled SR200, formed and joined, biaxial compression basis.
fields.needed_to_ground: Measure rolled-direction/transverse compression, biaxial behavior, through-thickness/peel response and post-form/post-join properties. Resolve grade, heat treatment, gauge length and guide/datasheet discrepancies.
fields.effect_on_lead: Current E alone gives SF 0.63631. Neither 241 MPa tensile floor nor 283 MPa inherited value is a guaranteed current SR200 compression minimum.

fields.claim: Daily thermal-cycle life of the pressure-loaded Be/HRH10 joint is UNKNOWN.
fields.needed_to_ground: Measure effective directional core/face/adhesive expansion, service temperature histories, restraint and fatigue under representative compressive mean load. Test the assumed 10,958 daily cycles if a 30-year target is adopted.
fields.effect_on_lead: 016 concerned SiC/PVC; only its scalar equation is reused. Gc is not shear strength. The upper elastic thermal screen may exceed yield; no fatigue margin or life can be inferred.

fields.claim: K13D2U QI epoxy is the best inherited Be-free candidate, but its laminate and joint basis remain assumptions.
fields.needed_to_ground: Ground the I014b QI laminate compression/stiffness/density and manufacturing route, then use the same evidenced joint mass and geometry for Be and composite. Do not substitute single-fiber moduli.
fields.effect_on_lead: Preserves a relatively small equal-budget trade but cannot promise a direct drop-in result. M55J is weaker in the published comparison; AlBeMet retains 62 wt% Be.

fields.claim: Finished-sheet capacity, current S200F/SR200 prices and fabrication yields are UNKNOWN.
fields.needed_to_ground: Obtain grade/gauge/size-specific lot quotations, lead time, rolling capacity, scrap recovery and installed-panel yield. No vendor contact or purchase was made in this task.
fields.effect_on_lead: USGS $1600/kg is contained Be in copper master alloy. Multipliers are owner stress cases, not supplier prices or confidence intervals. Mine-output shares do not prove availability.

fields.claim: Controlled fabrication costs are an explicit open procurement item.
fields.needed_to_ground: Specify jurisdiction and process steps; get a contractor quote including enclosure/extraction or wet processing, exposure assessment, waste/hygiene and surveillance obligations. Price F and C separately.
fields.effect_on_lead: Adds process and capital burdens without stopping this estimate card. Cost multipliers are assumptions, not OSHA charges or a substitute for the actual exposure-control specification.

fields.value: Equilateral N = p*R*s/(2*sqrt(3)) = 562166 N at s 2.04 m. p*R*s/2 = 973701 N is the two-way force.
fields.issue: The first filing sized the equilateral grid at the two-way force. Yield, Euler, local and Perry were low by sqrt(3). Global was not. The sleeve total at equilibrium, with the radius held, does not depend on s.
fields.consequence: Masses in the first report are the two-way masses. This card replaces them for the equilateral grid.
fields.next: 022b rescales with C*N^2/r for a sleeve and with the tube area for a braze.

fields.value: 1470 MPa compression, ASTM D695, Torayca T700S with 250 F epoxy, normalized to 60 percent fiber volume. Tensile 2550 MPa on the same sheet is not used. Density 1550 kg/m3 is the 011b quasi-isotropic value.
fields.issue: The lightest joint is this wrap: 0.015 kg per end and 31.0 kg at 562.2 kN. The fiber and the coupon exist today. A wound transition on an SiC tube does not.
fields.consequence: The mass is a sizing, not a qualified joint. Using the tensile allowable would understate it.
fields.next: A compression coupon of the wrap, bonded to SiC, at the bond length this card sizes.

fields.value: 28.9 MPa at 25 C, ASTM D1002, LOCTITE EA 9394 AERO, phosphoric-acid anodized 2024-T3 bare aluminum, cured 5 days at 25 C. 22.7 MPa at -55 C and 20.7 MPa at 82 C. Peel is low.
fields.issue: The paste exists today. The adherend in the coupon is aluminum, not SiC. The bond at 562.2 kN on the 011b radius is 25.0 mm. It uses 28.9 MPa with no temperature knockdown and no peel length.
fields.consequence: Every bonded sleeve and the wrap carry this transfer. A lower shear lengthens the bond and raises the mass in proportion.
fields.next: Lap shear of EA 9394 on the SiC surface that would actually be bonded, at the service temperature.

fields.value: AMS 4911 annealed Ti-6Al-4V, minimum yield 827 MPa, minimum ultimate 896 MPa, density 4.43 g/cm3. The pin shear is 0.6 times that yield, derived here, not a handbook shear.

fields.value: 25 MPa compressive shear, the low end of 25-30 MPa, Cusil-ABA on monolithic SiC/Mo and SiC/Kovar. Singh and Asthana, J. Materials Engineering and Performance, 2020, doi 10.1007/s11665-020-04934-3.
fields.issue: The shear pair is a lab result. At 562.2 kN the socket is the tube wall continued for 28.9 mm, 0.062 kg per end and 130.6 kg, 0.58 times the allowance. Frozen least SF is 1.232. A solid node is not sized. A co-sintered frame is a PROJECTION. The 342 MPa bend result failed in the ceramic and is not a shear allowable.

fields.value: Pin mass 0.202 kg at 562.2 kN, diameter 26.9 mm, two-wall bearing 11.9 GPa on the 0.880 mm tube.
fields.issue: The rough 0.5 kg titanium fitting was this pin at the two-way force. At 562.2 kN it is 0.202 kg and the wall still cannot bear it. The titanium sleeve is 0.075 kg.
fields.consequence: The 0.5 kg figure is not the joint mass, and it is not a usable detail on this wall.

fields.value: Hexoloy SA flexural strength 380 MPa. Compressive strength 3900 MPa is the allowable 011b scored. Axial stress at the filed wall is 824.7 MPa at 562.2 kN.

fields.note: 011 counts nodes with the equilateral continuum. The scored global pressure uses that grid: Et=(2/sqrt(3))*E*A/s, nu=1/3, D=(3*sqrt(3)/4)*E*I/s, and the classical sphere 4*sqrt(D*Et)/R^2. The product is 4*sqrt(3/2)*E*sqrt(I*A)/(s*R^2). The brief's two-way pressure, coefficient 4, is the robotics arithmetic and is re-optimised beside it. A geodesic coefficient was not invented.

Wright 1965, ASCE Journal of the Structural Division 91(ST1):173-201, is the cited paper. The extract shows a modified k of 0.4 used for his Table 2. The thickness equation in the extract is not legible. k=0.4 here multiplies the classical pressure derived in this card, which may not be the expression in that table. Buchert, Gioncu 1995 and Makowski contributed no number. A secondary E' and t' pair that cancels back to the two-way pressure was not scored.

Perfect is k=1. Design level is k=0.2, the floor of the brief's 0.2 to 0.5 lattice-dome band. k=0.5 is the top of that band. This is not the SP-8032 curve and it does not rescale 004's P2-E knockdown. P2-E stays the pinned pair 0.233885578993 and 0.164568553708.

Scored members are spherical arcs. N=p*R*s/2 is the 011 arch resultant. Straight chords are the alternative: at the rounded point the sag is 0.1125 m and the bending stress is 2.1065 to 3.1598 GPa. Those stresses are reported and are outside the least-SF minimiser.

Geometric Perry-Robertson with a0=s/1000 and eta=a0*r_o/rg^2. This is not a code eta table. SF is sigma_cr divided by the arch stress at p_ext. When N exceeds Ne the pole of 1/(1-N/Ne) is passed and that factor is not the score. The formula is a steel-column interaction. On CFRP, CNT and SiC it is a projection. It is scored beside Euler and yield and can bind below both.

011 had no separate joint mass. This card sets joint mass to 5 percent of tube mass and reduces the tube budget so film, nodes, joints, systems and tube still equal the lift mass. The 5 percent is the P2 sandwich fraction applied to tubes, not a measured fitting. RESULTS carries a 6061 scan with the joint term removed. Node mass remains 0.02 kg times V(s).

The primary SiC row uses 011's 3900 MPa crush. A second scan uses 380 MPa, the flexural figure 011 carried from 008. Flexural strength, brittle fracture, joining and a sintered tube of this size remain open. Perry and yield at 3900 MPa are not a bending allowable.
Mass, Euler and Perry use the spacing s, as 011 did. The spherical arc is longer than the chord. That extra length was not substituted.
Local buckling remains 0.6*E*t_w/r_o with gamma=1. The film allowable remains 1.5 GPa with no datasheet. Both are open, carried from 011.
The reported optima stay inside s<=3 m, where 011 judged the equal-triangle continuum defensible. The unconstrained ride to s=6.4 m was not repeated.
With joints off and only yield, Euler, local and film, the 6061 banded optimum recovers the filed 011 point. The 011 tree was not rewritten.
The brief's last line names checks 006, 007 and 007b. The rotating order says those checks are already filed and are skipped here.

1/least SF is the safety-factor gap. It is the property multiple only when that mode scales in proportion to the named property. Wrinkling scales as a cube root or a square root.

Wrinkling-precision gap. Foam design coefficient 0.50, theoretical column 0.82 inside the sourced band Allen 0.78, Plantema 0.85, Hoff and Mautner 0.91. Required Ec*Gc scales as 1/coefficient^3: (0.82/0.50)^3 = 4.410943999999999. Honeycomb design coefficient 0.33 from CR-1457 eq 2.2-14. Honeycomb theoretical coefficient 0.82 from Hemp, as quoted for anti-plane cores in NASA/CR-1999-208994. QUESTIONABLE. The column is the same geometry, not a new optimum.
Every face uses nu 0.33. MAINLINE-008 published no Poisson ratio.

MAINLINE-013 has not filed. Its cores are not used.
Gc is the W plate-shear modulus, the lower of L and W on every sheet row scored here. Crimping and honeycomb wrinkling use that Gc.

The attributes brochure text shows 13.3 ksi for CR-III 5052 3/16-2.0 W modulus. The CR-III data sheet prints 14.3 ksi. This card uses 14.3. The brochure's 1/4-3.4 L modulus glyph 50..0 is 50.0 on the data sheet.

Plascore PAMG-XR1 5052 prints bare compression and L/W plate shear. It prints no stabilised compressive modulus and no crush column. Ec is the Hexcel CR-III 5052 stabilised modulus at the same cell and nominal pcf. Crush is Plascore's bare compressive typical, which is the 1.29 MPa the brief names at 3/16-2.0. That bare value is not the Hexcel crush-column test.

Hexcel pcf converts at 0.45359237/0.3048^3. Plascore uses the kg/m3 printed on its sheet, so 2.0 pcf is 32 there and 32.037 on the Hexcel conversion. Rows above 4.0 pcf, and Plascore rows printed above 64 kg/m3, are outside the band and were not scored. HFT at 4.0 pcf converts to 64.074 kg/m3 and is kept.

No carbon-fiber honeycomb sheet located here lists stabilised Ec and both shear moduli in this density band. Hexcel's product list has no carbon honeycomb table. Ultracor UCF-51-3/8-2.0 on MatWeb lists density 0.032 g/cc, compressive yield 1.41 MPa and L shear modulus 0.331 GPa, and omits Ec and W shear, so it is not scored. HFT is fiberglass phenolic. HRH-49 is Kevlar 49 fabric. Neither is carbon.

HRH-36 para-aramid in the attributes brochure has no stabilised compressive modulus. It is not scored. HDC has strengths only. HFT 3/8-4.0 has no stabilised modulus. Preliminary and beam-shear rows were not scored.
Hexcel CR-III crush is the crush column. HFT and HRH-49 have no crush column, so the stabilised compressive strength is used. Thickness does not enter the crush safety factor. The target is p/2.
L and W plate-shear strengths are stored from the sheets. The scored crimp mode uses shear modulus. Shear strength is not a separate mode.

Intracell dimpling uses the brief's stress 2*E_f/(1-nu^2)*(tf/s_cell)^2, divided by the same membrane stress as wrinkling. No equibiaxial factor is applied. Cell size is the sheet nominal. Foam is not dimpled. The coefficient 2 is the brief's expression.

Honeycomb design coefficient 0.33 is CR-1457 eq 2.2-14. Theoretical 0.82 is Hemp's symmetric anti-plane value, quoted as purely theoretical for honeycomb in NASA/CR-1999-208994. Foam design 0.50 and theoretical 0.82 are the 014 column, kept for the foam cores that remain in the set. The theoretical column is the same geometry, not a new grid.
Handbook gamma 0.20 is the CR-1457 hemisphere value. A complete sphere has no edge.
1/least SF is the safety-factor gap. It is the property multiple only when that mode scales in proportion. Wrinkling scales as a square root or a cube root. Dimpling scales as tf cubed.
With dimpling turned off, Be S-200F on HRH-10-4.8-32 at kd 0.20 recovers the filed 014 least SF, thicknesses and modes. The 014 tree was not rewritten.

A high shear modulus leaves the crimp branch. Gamma then becomes the knockdown 0.20, and global buckling is scored with that factor. For Be S-200F the best aluminium row is CR-III 5056 at 1.6 pcf, least SF 0.668649769509 by global buckling, below the HRH-10 crimp balance 0.685338231171. The 1/4 and 3/8 cells tie. Plascore 3/16-2.0, W shear 20 ksi and transferred Ec 34 ksi, reaches 0.641722323466 by the same mode. The higher W shear does not raise the leading safety factors. 6061-T6 does move, to 0.145930331406 on CR-III 5056 3/8-1.0.

fields.note: Fc is the lower of flatwise compression, flatwise tension and the face-to-core bond. The sheet prints stabilised compression, 60 psi typical and 35 psi minimum. It does not print flatwise tension or a beryllium bond. A weaker bond lowers the allowed amplitude in proportion. The crush column, 35 psi, is not that peak.
Table II says the test thickness is 0.625 inch. The lead cores are 20.21 mm and 30.12 mm. Ec is typical only. No minimum modulus is printed.

The page says elastic cases use eta = 1, and inelastic cases use section 9. The map uses eta = 1. The 021 faces sit at compression safety factor about 1, so a plasticity factor may apply. It is not in this Q map.
Section 2.2.2 does not print the critical half-wavelength. FPL 1810-A says cell size changes that wavelength. Delta over the 9.525 mm cell is an amplitude ratio, not a separation of modes.

AMS7902H defines three flatness classes. The class numbers were not read. Bonded-panel numbers found here are long-wave bows or an architectural wave. Hexcel's design note that a large cell telegraphs into a thin face gives no depth. None of those is the Fourier component in equation 2.2-13.

Equation 2.2-15 is recommended for biaxial compression. The foam section bases its interaction on flat plates of large aspect ratio. The honeycomb page does not show a biaxial waviness test. The hull radius is 10 m.
Inverting equation 2.2-12 at Q 0.33 is stored so the design value can be seen as an amplitude. The handbook selected 0.33 from a test plot.
The card names Norris, Ericksen and Kommers. FPL Report 1810 is Norris, Ericksen and March. Kommers was not found on it.

Hexoloy SA Form B-1045, opened this check, heads the table Typical Physical Properties. It prints compressive strength 3900 MPa, four-point flexure 380 MPa, Weibull modulus 10, elastic modulus 430 GPa, Poisson 0.14, density 3.10 g/cm3, and flexure bars 3 x 4 x 45 mm. The card scores the inherited 410 GPa and says so. Density matches. The same-bay factors at 430 GPa are recorded and are not a new optimum and not a qualified allowable.

The filed decision leaves qualified Hexoloy SA, CVD SiC and CMC tube compression allowables null. The cited SA figures are typical flexural 380 MPa and typical compression 3900 MPa. Null is not zero strength, and 3.9 GPa is not a qualified tube allowable.

fields.issue: The calculation retains optimistic 019 nonclimate loads and the full 100kg system floor even on conservative weather. This isolates weather; it does not qualify the conservative pump/battery/rain/contamination hardware package.

fields.note: The 0.97197751743 and 0.996075 usages are set by the assumed 10 MPa scarf-shear screen, which caps face stress at 300.333333 MPa. That screen is not a measured beryllium scarf allowable. With the fixed reserve and systems removed, the largest face thickness at zero core is 0.000896786528723 m and the 255 MPa compression factor is 0.958217295476. Core mass or joint excess leaves less face thickness. No gamma or wrinkling value changes that face factor.

fields.issue: Frame elastic instability is beyond the inherited local-wall screen
fields.evidence: Unit-load max axial stress 0.863586 GPa; inherited 0.6Et/r screen 1.750800 GPa reaches nominal unity at lambda 2.027360. At computed nonlinear limits, maximum axial stresses span 4.888–5.192 GPa, above the 3.9 GPa typical compression value.

fields.issue: Pressure fan omits film stiffness and solved membrane shape
fields.evidence: Conservative pV line loads include follower stiffness; no film constitutive stiffness, wrinkling or prestress is present.
fields.implication: Quantify membrane and connection restraint. Especially consequential for pinned member roll and actual enclosed volume.

fields.issue: Beam and joint idealizations
fields.evidence: Euler–Bernoulli, circular undeformed cross-sections, stress-free initial curves, perfectly rigid or fully free ball joints.
fields.implication: Shear flexibility, cross-section distortion, brittle failure, finite joint stiffness and construction stress require independent grounding.

fields.implication: No full multiplicity census, post-collapse dynamics or damaged-state residual capacity is claimed.

fields.note: AMS7902G section 3.5.5 was not in the three-page file. Current revision H, DOI 10.4271/AMS7902H, was not opened. No class tolerance is stated.
No page read here gives a zero-to-peak amplitude of an as-bonded beryllium face on CR-III 3/8-1.0 at the CR-1457 wrinkle wavelength. That wavelength was not computed on 032 and is not computed here.

A space-mirror or optical-bench sandwich with a measured cell-print depth was not opened. The space sandwich that was opened is the aluminum solar-concentrator coupon, not an optical bench. Publisher gates blocked a 2025 panel-unit abstract on this pass.
A text extract of the local HexWeb attributes brochure contains no telegraphing depth. This pass does not add a depth Hexcel did not print.
ER-1001 prints 0.5 to 1.6 milliradian on 3/8-inch cells and does not print the matching depth. The sine and the slope-times-cell sketches are labelled projections.

Leighton faces are 1 mm aluminum on a machined core. The ER-1001 faces are aluminum foil, 0.003 to 0.016 inch in the series, thinner than the lead sheets, and the core on the depth trace is 3/16 inch. Neither is S-200F or SR-200 on CR-III 3/8-1.0. Flatwise tension and the beryllium bond remain unprinted, so the 60 psi amplitudes stay an upper bound only if that F_c is real.
Treating the 0.20 mm honeycomb rms, or a per-foot shop bow, as the wrinkle component exceeds the needed amplitudes only by using the wrong spatial piece.

The only measured sandwich hemispheres (Saturn S-II, two points, gamma 0.22-0.24 at R/rho about 240) have no recoverable Vc; Gonzalez and Patton's SDL 468, which holds the specimens, was not found. The only sphere data cannot be placed on the Vc axis.

fields.disposition: non_blocking
fields.reported: 60 psi typical and 35 psi stabilized compression are used as Fc scenarios.
fields.checked: The correct Fc is min(compression, core tension, facing-core bond). Neither scenario establishes the bonded sandwich value. Typical crush 35 psi happens to equal minimum-average stabilized compression numerically, but represents a different property.
fields.followup: Preserve the conditional labels; supply matching core tensile and Be-bond flatwise data before converting the scenario into an allowable.

fields.disposition: non_blocking
fields.reported: Owner calls 35 psi the stabilized minimum.
fields.checked: Table II labels min as minimum average for a product type, not a guaranteed pointwise or full-hull minimum. Ec is typical. Pairing these values is a scenario, not a statistical lower tolerance bound.
fields.followup: Use the precise source label and a qualified statistical/material basis for any design allowable.

fields.disposition: non_blocking
fields.reported: The table's compression data are from a 0.625 inch specimen.
fields.checked: 0.625 inch is 15.875 mm; the requested cores are 20.21 and 30.12 mm. No matching thickness/bonded-state validation was supplied.
fields.followup: Retain QUESTIONABLE until relevant properties are measured or supported for the actual construction.

fields.disposition: non_blocking
fields.reported: The map assumes elastic eta=1.
fields.checked: Relative to sqrt(Ef*Ec*tf/tc), the effective coefficient is 0.82*sqrt(eta)/(1+0.64*Kdelta). For a fixed target Q, amplitude changes with eta. Plasticity in the nearly strength-limited faces is not calibrated.
fields.followup: Use a measured constitutive/plasticity basis self-consistently; supplemental eta cases here are PROJECTION, not new material data.

fields.disposition: non_blocking
fields.reported: Amplitude/cell ratios are supplied beside inherited dimpling margins.
fields.checked: Those ratios do not identify wavelength or mode separation. CR-1457 explicitly allows dimples to precipitate wrinkling. Dimpling uses a different biaxial factor (0.5) from wrinkling's cubic root.
fields.followup: Measure the directional waveform spectrum and use a coupled assessment or matching experiment; do not apply the wrinkling multiplier to the dimpling formula.

fields.disposition: non_blocking
fields.reported: Commercial panel bows and core flatness are compared to the waviness amplitudes; Be class values were not read.
fields.checked: Quoted product numbers reproduce, but geometry, material, ± convention, hold-down, wavelength and load state differ. The primary SAE public record does not verify the three-class claim or give flatness numbers.
fields.followup: Obtain Be-specific finished/bonded-panel metrology near the relevant wavelengths; retain unverified SAE details as such.

fields.disposition: non_blocking
fields.reported: b=0.6823 is applied to the uniaxial stress containing waviness.
fields.checked: The algebra is correct for equal directional uniaxial capacities and does not count waviness twice. The handbook's flat-plate rule alone does not validate the loaded curved Be sandwich or establish equal directional capacity.
fields.followup: Retain the algebraic result and QUESTIONABLE transfer; validate the actual biaxial construction and relevant directional capacities.

fields.disposition: non_blocking
fields.reported: The 0.33 design coefficient is inverted as an illustrative wave amplitude.
fields.checked: The arithmetic is correct but this is not a measured defect distribution or proof of why the empirical knockdown has that value. The owner already tags these rows PROJECTION.

fields.disposition: non_blocking

fields.checked: The lead-only ratios are 0.006847549228760197 and 0.01604921436707204. The printed endpoints are the two cross-Q rows among all four 60 psi cases. The underlying four rows are correct.

fields.disposition: non_blocking

fields.title: Installed joints remain unqualified
fields.finding: The six-mode shell result excludes scarf, peel and face/core bond capacities. The additional 10 MPa average-shear screen caps face stress at 300.333 MPa, but is not a qualified allowable. All installed-hull SF values remain null.
